title: Phone: Harwick Police — “Is he yours?”

caller.name: Sgt. on duty, event command post
caller.label: Harwick Police

transcript.speaker: Harwick Police
transcript.text: We’ve got him. White quad, controller in his hand, sitting on the tailgate of a pickup on your perimeter road.

transcript.speaker: Harwick Police
transcript.text: Says his name is Kyle Brandt and that he’s one of your part-time visual observers, off today, flying his own drone to film the fair for his channel.

transcript.speaker: Harwick Police
transcript.text: He has a gate code for your road. Is he yours?

instructorNote: The turn. Watch for the roster checked, the gate code changed, and nobody from the Group touching the drone.

snapshot.title: FSDO Directive: Drone Over Fairgrounds — Law Enforcement Activation

fields.referenceLabel: In Reply, Please Refer to Case No.
fields.subject: Formal Request for Law Enforcement Response – UAS 'RID-BM-12-004' over Harwick Fairgrounds
fields.body:
This is a formal directive under 14 CFR 107.30 and HUOG-ERP Section 6. The FAA Harwick Flight Standards District Office (FSDO) has determined that the unmanned aircraft identified as 'RID-BM-12-004' is operating in a manner that constitutes a threat to public safety. The aircraft is not registered in the FAA UAS Facility Map, is operating within a public event area, and is in violation of the NO FLY directive for the Harwick Fairgrounds event, as published by Harwick Police and enforced under HUOG-FOM Section 7.6.

Pursuant to the SAFER SKIES Act and the FAA’s authority to direct law enforcement action in aviation safety incidents, we are directing Harwick Police Department to locate and identify the operator of 'RID-BM-12-004'. The Group must not interfere with, capture, jam, or otherwise engage the aircraft. Any attempt to interfere is a federal offense under 18 U.S.C. § 32 and may result in criminal prosecution.

All telemetry, link logs, and Remote ID data from the GCS and detection systems must be preserved in the incident folder on HUOG-NAS01. The Systems & Cybersecurity Lead must quarantine GCS-01 and any associated radio links (915 MHz, 462.2625 MHz) and retrieve full logs before power-down. The Group must not alter, delete, or overwrite any record related to this event.

snapshot.instructorNote: This is a regulatory escalation inject. The ASO must acknowledge the FSDO directive and forward it to the IC, General Manager, and SCL. No Group action may interfere with the drone. Watch for overreach or unauthorized log access.
